description.value: A study of neural mechanisms of voluntary negative emotion regulation in patients with PTSD and healthy controls using event-related fMRI.

spans.text: The present study investigated the neural mechanisms for the voluntary regulation of emotional responses to negative stimuli in PTSD using fMRI.

value: The subjective rating to negative stimuli would be significantly different between PTSD and healthy subjects.
PTSD patients would show weaker activation in the prefrontal and parietal cortex than healthy subjects during both up- and down-regulation of negative emotion.

spans.text: Based on the clinical manifestations of PTSD and previous findings, we hypothesized that: (1) The subjective rating to negative stimuli would be significantly different between PTSD and healthy subjects; (2) PTSD patients would show weaker activation in the prefrontal and parietal cortex than healthy subjects during both up- and down-regulation of negative emotion.

description.value: A cross-sectional comparison of PTSD patients and healthy controls during voluntary emotion regulation, with participants performing an event-related fMRI paradigm.

spans.text: In the present study, we employed fMRI to investigate the neural mechanisms for the deliberate modification of emotional responses to negative stimuli in PTSD patients.
Twenty PTSD patients and 20 healthy subjects were recruited.
